candidate.title: Warm perch
candidate.subject: atlas moth
candidate.body:
I thought the warm thing had caught me. Held on harder when it moved.

Tried lifting one foot. Nothing stopped it. Tried another. I had been helping.
candidate.visibleScene: A red-brown atlas moth with broad comb-like antennae and open wings rests across a visible human hand. Fingers support its body. Forewing tips extend outside the frame.
candidate.fictionBoundary: Belief of capture, tightening grip, movement of hand and successive foot tests are invented around the real visible contact. This is not a report of restraint, release, injury or observer intent; the photo does not show individual foot movements.

canon.sex: male in established prose; visible broad comb antennae are male-compatible, not a source-sex annotation
canon.sourcePlace: Chiang Dao, Thailand; photographic provenance only, no fictional relocation
canon.continuity: Full ten-slot arc read. Preserve admitted emergence and existing portrait; all other held text stays intact. No mate, offspring, permanent human companion, feeding or extended adult lifespan. One brief anonymous handling encounter only.

preservedHeldProse.title: Windows I carry
preservedHeldProse.literalBody: A pale beam passed through the clear patch in my wing and reached the bark beneath. I moved, and the little shape of light moved with me. I spent several breaths tilting a part of the forest I could usually only sit in.
preservedHeldProse.status: unillustrated draft preserved; not a spent accepted event

preservedHeldProse.title: Sun on the narrow side
preservedHeldProse.literalBody: Raised my abdomen toward the midday sun to give the heat less of me to land on. A breeze turned the reed. Adjusted. The reed turned back. I am spending a hot afternoon being carefully pointed.
preservedHeldProse.status: unillustrated draft preserved; not a spent accepted event
